title: Inviting, requesting and asking permission
title_target: 一起去吧 — Yìqǐ qù ba
goal: Tell apart 会, 能 and 可以 — all three often translated "can"; express wishes with 想 and 要; and invite, ask for help and say no politely.
bekal: use 会, 能 and 可以 each in its place
tell 想 (would like) from 要 (want, will)
invite with 吧 and 我们一起…
ask for help with 请 and 帮

dialogs.title: 对话 1 — A dinner invitation
dialogs.intro: Li Ming invites Andi and Wang Li to dinner. Notice three different words that all come out as "can" in English.

lines.speaker: 李明:
lines.id: Let's have dinner together tonight!
lines.literal: evening — we — together — eat — rice — (suggestion).

lines.speaker: 王丽:
lines.id: Sure! Where shall we eat?
lines.literal: good — (softener). go — where — eat.

lines.speaker: 李明:
lines.text: [学校|Xuéxiào][旁边|pángbiān][有|yǒu][一|yì][家|jiā][新|xīn][饭馆|fànguǎn]，[听说|tīngshuō][不错|búcuò]。
lines.id: There's a new restaurant next to the school — I hear it's pretty good.
lines.literal: school — beside — have — one — (classifier) — new — restaurant, hear-say — not — wrong.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [对不起|Duìbuqǐ]，[我|wǒ][今天|jīntiān][不|bù][能|néng][去|qù]。[我|Wǒ][有|yǒu][课|kè]。
lines.id: Sorry, I can't go today. I have class.
lines.literal: sorry, I — today — not — able — go. I — have — class.

lines.speaker: 李明:
lines.text: [几|Jǐ][点|diǎn][下课|xià kè]？[我们|Wǒmen][可以|kěyǐ][等|děng][你|nǐ]。
lines.id: What time does your class end? We can wait for you.
lines.literal: how-many — o'clock — go-down — class. we — may — wait — you.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.id: Eight. That's too late, isn't it?
lines.literal: eight — o'clock. too — late — (change) — right.

lines.speaker: 王丽:
lines.id: It's not late. That restaurant is open until ten.
lines.literal: not — late. that — (classifier) — restaurant — open — until — ten — o'clock.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [那|Nà][好|hǎo][吧|ba]。[我|Wǒ][下课|xià kè][以后|yǐhòu][给|gěi][你们|nǐmen][打|dǎ][电话|diànhuà]。
lines.id: Okay then. I'll call you after class.
lines.literal: that — good — (softener). I — go-down — class — after — to — you-all — hit — phone.

lines.speaker: 李明:
lines.text: [你|Nǐ][能|néng][吃|chī][辣|là][的|de][吗|ma]？[那|Nà][家|jiā][是|shì][四川菜|Sìchuān cài]。
lines.id: Can you handle spicy food? That place does Sichuan food.
lines.literal: you — able — eat — spicy — (one) — (question). that — (classifier) — be — Sichuan — dish.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.id: I can, but not anything too spicy.
lines.literal: able, but — not — able — eat — too — spicy — (one).

lines.speaker: 王丽:
lines.id: No problem, we can order dishes that aren't spicy.
lines.literal: not-have — problem, may — order — not — spicy — (of) — dish.

notes: **[吧|ba] turns a statement into an invitation.** [我们一起吃饭吧|Wǒmen yìqǐ chī fàn ba]！ = let's eat together. Without 吧, the same sentence sounds like an announcement.

**⚠️ [不能|bù néng] = can't because of circumstances; [不会|bú huì] = can't because you never learned.** [我不能去|Wǒ bù néng qù] I can't go (something's in the way); [我不会开车|Wǒ bú huì kāi chē] I can't drive (never learned). Swapping them changes the meaning completely.
**[可以|kěyǐ] expresses permission or possibility.** [我们可以等你|Wǒmen kěyǐ děng nǐ] we can (don't mind) wait for you; [可以坐这儿吗|Kěyǐ zuò zhèr ma]？ may I sit here?
**[不错|búcuò] literally "not wrong", meaning "pretty good".** One of the most common compliments in Chinese — warmer than it sounds.
**[家|jiā] is the classifier for businesses**: restaurants, shops, companies, hotels. [一家饭馆|yì jiā fànguǎn], [两家公司|liǎng jiā gōngsī].

**Adjective + [的|de] replaces a noun that's already clear.** [辣的|là de] = the spicy one(s), [不辣的|bú là de] = the non-spicy one(s), [贵的|guì de] = the expensive one(s). Very common when ordering food or shopping.
**[下课以后|xià kè yǐhòu] = after class.** ⚠️ The order is the reverse of English: the event first, then 以后. Likewise [吃饭以前|chī fàn yǐqián] before eating.

grammars.title: 会, 能, 可以 — three different "cans"
body: This is one of the hardest points for learners, because English uses "can" for all three. Tell them apart by the **reason** the ability exists or doesn't.

head: Word
Reason
Example
Meaning
rows: **Circumstances** allow it: time, energy, health, opportunity
[我今天不能来|Wǒ jīntiān bù néng lái]。
[我能吃三碗|Wǒ néng chī sān wǎn]。

head: English sentence
Correct form
Reason
rows: I can't drive today (I've been drinking).
[今天我不能开车|Jīntiān wǒ bù néng kāi chē]。
[这儿可以开车吗|Zhèr kěyǐ kāi chē ma]？
[我不会游泳|Wǒ bú huì yóu yǒng]。
I can't swim today (I have the flu).
[今天我不能游泳|Jīntiān wǒ bù néng yóu yǒng]。

after: ⚠️ To **refuse permission**, use [不能|bù néng] or [不行|bù xíng], not 不可以. 不可以 sounds harsh, like scolding a small child.
Short answers echo the word in the question: [你会吗|Nǐ huì ma]？ → [会|Huì]。 [你能吗|Nǐ néng ma]？ → [能|Néng]。 [可以吗|Kěyǐ ma]？ → [可以|Kěyǐ]。

grammars.title: 想 and 要 — would like and want

head: Word
Nuance
Example
rows: Would like, feel like — soft, not necessarily going to happen
[我想去中国|Wǒ xiǎng qù Zhōngguó]。 I'd like to go to China.
Want, be going to — firm, already decided
[我要去中国|Wǒ yào qù Zhōngguó]。 I'm going to China.
[我要一杯茶|Wǒ yào yì bēi chá]。 I'll have a tea.
[要下雨了|Yào xià yǔ le]。 It's about to rain.
[我想要一个新手机|Wǒ xiǎngyào yí ge xīn shǒujī]。

after: ⚠️ **The negative of 要 isn't 不要 but 不想.** [我不想去|Wǒ bù xiǎng qù] = I don't want to go. [我不要去|Wǒ bú yào qù] sounds like a sulking child or a blunt refusal.
⚠️ [不要|bú yào] before a verb means **"don't"**, not "don't want": [不要走|Bú yào zǒu] don't go. A shorter synonym: [别|bié].

dialogs.title: 对话 2 — Asking for help
dialogs.intro: Andi needs Wang Li's help. Notice that every request is wrapped first — Chinese people rarely ask for something directly without a lead-in.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [王丽|Wáng Lì]，[你|nǐ][现在|xiànzài][有空|yǒu kòng][吗|ma]？
lines.id: Wang Li, are you free right now?
lines.literal: Wang Li, you — now — have — free-time — (question).

lines.speaker: 王丽:
lines.id: Yes, what's up?
lines.literal: have, what — matter.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.id: I'd like to ask you a favor.
lines.literal: I — would-like — ask — you — help — (classifier) — busy.

lines.speaker: 王丽:
lines.id: Go ahead.
lines.literal: you — speak — (suggestion).

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [你|Nǐ][能|néng][帮|bāng][我|wǒ][看看|kànkan][这|zhè][封|fēng][信|xìn][吗|ma]？[我|Wǒ][有|yǒu][几|jǐ][个|ge][字|zì][不|bú][认识|rènshi]。
lines.id: Could you take a look at this letter for me? There are a few characters I don't know.
lines.literal: you — able — help — me — look-look — this — (classifier) — letter — (question). I — have — a-few — (classifier) — character — not — know.

lines.speaker: 王丽:
lines.id: Of course. Let me see.
lines.literal: of-course — may. give — me — look-look.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [谢谢|Xièxie]！[还有|Háiyǒu]，[你|nǐ][可以|kěyǐ][教|jiāo][我|wǒ][怎么|zěnme][写|xiě][我的|wǒ de][中文|Zhōngwén][名字|míngzi][吗|ma]？
lines.id: Thanks! Oh, and could you teach me how to write my Chinese name?
lines.literal: thank. also, you — may — teach — me — how — write — my — Chinese — name — (question).

lines.speaker: 王丽:
lines.id: No problem! You already have a Chinese name?
lines.literal: not-have — problem. you — have — Chinese — name — (change).

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [有|Yǒu]，[我的|wǒ de][老师|lǎoshī][给|gěi][我|wǒ][起|qǐ][了|le][一|yí][个|ge]：[安迪|Āndí]。
lines.id: Yes, my teacher gave me one: An Di.
lines.literal: have, my — teacher — for — me — raise — (done) — one — (classifier): An Di.

lines.speaker: 王丽:
lines.id: It sounds nice! Here, I'll write it out for you.
lines.literal: (prop) — nice-to-hear. come, I — write — give — you — look.

notes: **[帮忙|bāng máng] = help, and it can be split.** [帮个忙|bāng ge máng] do a favor; [帮我一个忙|bāng wǒ yí ge máng] do me a favor. ⚠️ When there's a person as the object, use **[帮|bāng] alone**: [帮我看看|bāng wǒ kànkan], not 帮忙我.

**[请你帮我…|qǐng nǐ bāng wǒ…] is the most polite request frame.** The longer the lead-in, the more polite it sounds: [我想请你帮个忙|Wǒ xiǎng qǐng nǐ bāng ge máng] — "I'd like to ask a favor" — is gentler than stating the request straight away.

**Doubling a verb makes it sound casual**: [看看|kànkan] take a look, [听听|tīngting], [想想|xiǎngxiang], [试试|shìshi]. Two-syllable verbs double as a whole: [休息休息|xiūxi xiūxi], [商量商量|shāngliang shāngliang].
**[封|fēng] is the classifier for letters.** [一封信|yì fēng xìn].
**[教|jiāo] = teach, [学|xué] = learn.** ⚠️ 教 here is first tone (*jiāo*, teach); with the fourth tone (*jiào*) it means "teaching, religion".
**[给|gěi] has many jobs**: give ([给我|gěi wǒ]), for/to ([给你打电话|gěi nǐ dǎ diànhuà]), and "so that … can see" ([写给你看|xiě gěi nǐ kàn]).
**Chinese names** are almost always given by a teacher or Chinese friend, not picked from a dictionary. The sound is chosen to resemble your real name, and the meaning to be a good one.

grammars.title: Inviting, requesting and declining

head: Purpose
Sentence
Nuance
rows: [我们一起去吧|Wǒmen yìqǐ qù ba]！
[要不要一起吃饭|Yào bu yào yìqǐ chī fàn]？
[你能帮我…吗|Nǐ néng bāng wǒ… ma]？
Sorry for the trouble — said afterward
[对不起，我有事|Duìbuqǐ, wǒ yǒu shì]。
[今天不太方便|Jīntiān bú tài fāngbiàn]。

after: ⚠️ **A bare "no" is considered rude.** The safe form always has three parts: **sorry + short reason + alternative**. [对不起，我今天有课，下次吧|Duìbuqǐ, wǒ jīntiān yǒu kè, xià cì ba]。 The reason can be short, but it has to be there.
[不太方便|bú tài fāngbiàn] "not very convenient" is a gentle refusal everyone understands without further explanation.

blocks.text: Every word in this table stands **before the main verb**, and each is negated with 不 placed in front. Once you've got the position down, you just pick the meaning.

head: Word
Meaning
Positive
Negative
rows: [我不喜欢看书|Wǒ bù xǐhuan kàn shū]

blocks.title: Choice questions — the liveliest way to ask
items: Repeat the verb with 不 in the middle: [你去不去|Nǐ qù bu qù]？ [你会不会|Nǐ huì bu huì]？ [好不好|Hǎo bu hǎo]？
For two-syllable words, you can drop the second syllable in the first half: [喜不喜欢|xǐ bu xǐhuan]？ [可不可以|kě bu kěyǐ]？
⚠️ This form **can't be combined with 吗**. [你去不去吗|Nǐ qù bu qù ma]？ is wrong.
It means exactly the same as 吗, but sounds friendlier and more spoken. Native speakers use it all day long.

sections.title: Invitations, gifts and the dinner table

blocks.text: Being invited to a meal by Chinese people is a sign of real acceptance, and some customs may differ from yours. The following will keep you from putting a foot wrong.

head: Sentence
When to use it
rows: "It's my treat." Whoever invites usually pays
"Let me get this." Used when fighting over the bill
Splitting the bill. Common among young people, rare at formal dinners
"Eat more!" Said by the host again and again
"I'm full." How to turn down more food
[我不能喝酒|Wǒ bù néng hē jiǔ]。
"I can't drink alcohol." Religious or health reasons are accepted without question

blocks.title: Gifts: dos and don'ts
items: **Fine and welcome**: tea, fruit, snacks from your home country, liquor (if you know they drink), something typical of your country.
⚠️ **Clocks** — [送钟|sòng zhōng] sounds the same as [送终|sòng zhōng] "attend someone's deathbed".
⚠️ **Umbrellas** — [伞|sǎn] sounds like [散|sàn] "break up".
⚠️ **Shoes** — [鞋|xié] sounds like [邪|xié] "evil, bad luck".
⚠️ **Sharp objects** (knives, scissors) symbolize cutting ties.
Gifts are usually **not opened in front of the giver**, and at first they'll be **declined once or twice** before being accepted. Offer again calmly; it's part of the etiquette.

exercises.prompt: Correct these sentences, then write the correct form in pīnyīn.
items: [我不会去，我今天有课|Wǒ bú huì qù, wǒ jīntiān yǒu kè]。
[我不要去|Wǒ bú yào qù]。

answers: 会 — 能 — 可以 — 会 — 能 — 会
想 — 要 — 不想 — 别 — 别
我们 一起 去 吧 — 你 能 帮 我 吗 — 我 想 请 你 帮 个 忙 — 对不起 我 今天 不 能 去 — 你 会 不 会 开车 — 这儿 可以 坐 吗

Wǒ bù néng qù, wǒ jīntiān yǒu kè. — Wǒ bù xiǎng qù. — Nǐ néng bāng wǒ ma? — Nǐ qù bu qù? — Wǒ huì shuō Zhōngwén.
wave: Review Unit 8: invite three imaginary people to do three different things, then turn down three imaginary invitations with the sorry + reason + alternative pattern. Saying no politely is a skill you'll use far more often than you think.
